substeps.caption: Copper corrosion on the CubXL, as DAL's copper screen lays it out (PR #180): four stations, S1 C71500 Cu-Ni, S2 C95800 NAB, S3 a DED pad, S4 a PTFE blank; Ben's 9-vial holder of stocks; three cups; 2 x 8 ICP-MS tubes; two tip racks. On the head: the capper, a P20 and a camera.
1 The CubXL's P20 (1-20 µL) takes a 20 µL tip from Ben's rack.
2 The capper lifts the seawater cap (ASTM D1141, no heavy metals). The P20 builds S1's well from 135 µL of it: 7 transfers of 19.3 µL, each dispensed from above the meniscus.
3 Sulfide last: 15 µL of the 10 mg/L S stock, with the same tip, makes 150 µL at 1 mg/L S. The tip goes to the waste.
4 The head camera checks for liquid outside the O-ring (2 min).
5 The capper carries the electrode cap (leak-free Ag/AgCl reference, Pt coil counter) from its park cup and sets it over S1's boss: no O-ring, two small lid magnets hold it. No tip on.

6 Cap on, head free: OCP 20 min, EIS at OCP 10 min, LPR ±10 mV, rest 5 min, a +50 mV hold for 10 min, OCP 5 min. EIS needs the requested potentiostat: the EZstat Pro has none, so until then OCP runs 30 min.
7 The magnet lifts the cap off S1. It is dipped in DI water, then seawater, and parked.
8 A new tip moves the well's 150 µL to tube 1 for ICP-MS, 8 transfers of 18.75 µL, then a 150 µL DI rinse the same way: 16 transfers.
9 Acidify at once: the capper opens the acid vial and the night's one acid tip adds 20 µL of 1 M HNO3 from above the rim: 320 µL at 62 mM HNO3. The acid tip goes back to rack 2.
10 The head camera images the spot. Next: S2. A spot is 67 min of deck time: eight wells (three pieces, two wells each, and S4's two blanks) take about 9 h of a 12 h night.

Cyclic polarization runs only on selected spots, and last on each: fill to EIS, then the scan, then its own tube. On every spot it would swamp the tube's copper (3.4 mC against the hold's 0.2-2.8 mC).
